title: Motion-triggered servo sweep
summary: An HC-SR501 PIR sees motion, the ESP32-S3 lights an LED and sweeps an SG90 servo.

placements.note: Straddles the gap: J1 in column b, J3 in column i, rows 1-22. Antenna end at row 1, USB end past row 22.

placements.position_hint: left of the breadboard, lens facing up/out
right of the breadboard, near row 45

steps.heading: Seat the ESP32-S3 across the gap
steps.body: Unplug USB. Press the DevKitC-1 into the breadboard so the left header (J1, starts with 3V3) goes in column b and the right header (J3, starts with G) in column i, rows 1 to 22. The antenna end sits at row 1. You'll have one free hole per pin on each side (columns a and j).
safety: Push straight down on both headers evenly so pins don't bend.
steps.check: Every pin is in a hole and the board sits flat; J1.1 (3V3) is in b1.

steps.heading: Run 5V and ground to the left rails
steps.body: Red jumper from a21 (the 5V pin's row) to the red + rail. Black jumper from a22 (G) to the blue − rail.
safety: 5V must never touch a GPIO row. Double-check a21 is the row labeled 5V.
steps.check: Red wire from the 5V row to +, black from G row to −.

steps.heading: Wire the PIR sensor
steps.body: Read the silkscreen on your HC-SR501 (VCC, OUT, GND; check, clones differ). Female-to-male jumpers: VCC to the + rail, GND to the − rail, OUT to a4 (GPIO4).
safety: The PIR needs 5V+ (4.5-20V). Its OUT is 3.3V, so it's safe for GPIO4.
steps.check: Three wires: red to +, black to −, green into a4.

steps.heading: Connect the servo
steps.body: Male-to-male jumpers into the servo plug: red to the + rail, brown to the − rail (black jumper), orange to a5 (GPIO5).
safety: If the board resets when the servo moves, add a 100-470 µF capacitor across the + and − rails (stripe to −) or give the servo its own 5V supply with a shared ground.
steps.check: Orange into a5, red on +, brown on −.

steps.heading: Add the LED and resistor
steps.body: Purple jumper from a6 (GPIO6) to a30. Bend the 220 Ω resistor between b30 and b34. LED long leg (anode) in c34, short leg (cathode) in c35. Black jumper from a35 to the − rail.
safety: LED needs the resistor in series; without it you can damage the LED and the pin.
steps.check: Row 30: purple + resistor. Row 34: resistor + LED long leg. Row 35: LED short leg + black.

steps.heading: Flash the sketch
steps.body: Plug USB into the UART port. Create a PlatformIO project with the platformio.ini and main.cpp below, then Upload. The PIR needs about a minute to settle, then wave a hand: the LED lights and the servo sweeps.
safety: If upload fails, hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT, retry.
steps.check: Serial monitor shows 'Warming up PIR'; after ~60 s motion makes the LED light and the servo sweep 0→180→0.

code.platformio.ini:
[env:esp32-s3-devkitc-1]
platform = espressif32
board = esp32-s3-devkitc-1
framework = arduino
monitor_speed = 115200
lib_deps = madhephaestus/ESP32Servo
; N16R8: if your board has 16 MB flash / octal PSRAM, add:
; board_build.arduino.memory_type = qio_opi
; board_upload.flash_size = 16MB
